provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: BECE ict marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to solve past BECE questions correctly, identify key ICT concepts in past questions.

Introduction:
Today we will review past BECE ICT questions. This builds on our earlier ICT theory and practical lessons.

Content:
Past BECE questions cover hardware, software, networks and internet safety. For example, a question might ask 'What is the function of RAM?' or 'List two input devices.' We will discuss common question types and how to approach them. Nigerian examples include questions about using mobile money like M-Pesa or accessing government services online.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to solve 10 past BECE questions. They will then swap papers and mark each other's work.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does BECE stand for?
2. List three types of computer storage.
3. How should you approach a question about computer viruses?
4. Why is practicing past questions important for exams?

Summary:
Past questions help us understand exam patterns and improve our performance.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full mock examination within time limits, identify their own areas of strength and weakness.

Introduction:
Today we will take a full mock examination. This follows our review of past questions and helps us prepare for the real BECE.

Content:
The mock exam will cover all ICT topics including hardware, software, networks, programming and internet safety. It will have the same format as the BECE with multiple choice, theory and practical sections. Time management is crucial - just like in the real exam. Nigerian examples might include questions about using computers in Nigerian businesses or accessing educational resources like the National Open University of Nigeria portal.

Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock examination under timed conditions. After completion, we will review answers together and discuss common mistakes.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the main purpose of taking a mock exam?
2. How did you manage your time during the mock exam?
3. Which section did you find most difficult and why?
4. What will you do differently in the next mock exam?

Summary:
Mock exams help us practice exam conditions and identify areas for improvement.

topics.title: Project: my web page
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives: The students should be able to create a simple web page using HTML, publish their web page online. Introduction: Today we will start creating our own web pages. This builds on our earlier lessons about internet technologies and web design. Content: A web page is a document that can be displayed on the internet. We will use HTML (HyperText Markup Language) to create basic web pages. HTML uses tags to structure content like headings, paragraphs and images. For example,

creates a heading and

creates a paragraph. Nigerian examples could include creating a web page about Nigerian culture, local foods or tourist attractions like the Zuma Rock. Class activity: Students will create a simple web page about themselves or their favorite Nigerian dish using HTML tags. They will then learn how to preview their page in a web browser. Evaluation questions: 1. What does HTML stand for? 2. Name three HTML tags you can use in a web page. 3. How can you preview your web page before publishing? 4. What information would you include on a web page about Nigerian music? Summary: Creating web pages helps us understand how websites work and develop practical coding skills.

topics.title: Practical exam prep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete practical ICT tasks within time limits, demonstrate proper file management skills.

Introduction:
Today we will practice for the practical exam portion. This follows our web page project and helps us prepare for BECE practical tasks.

Content:
The practical exam tests your ability to perform common computer tasks. These include creating documents, spreadsheets, presentations and managing files. For example, you might be asked to create a budget for a small Nigerian business using spreadsheet software or organize photos in folders. Time management is crucial - practice completing tasks quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

Class activity:
Students will complete three timed practical tasks: 1) Create a document about Nigerian festivals, 2) Build a simple spreadsheet for a small business, 3) Create a presentation about Nigerian heroes.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three common practical tasks in ICT exams?
2. How can you save time when creating documents?
3. Why is file management important in practical exams?
4. What strategies will you use to stay calm during the practical exam?

Summary:
Practical exam preparation helps us build confidence and improve our performance in real exam conditions.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their own weak areas in ICT, practice targeted exercises to improve those areas.

Introduction:
Today we will focus on improving our weak areas. This follows our mock exams and practical preparation to address specific challenges.

Content:
Everyone has different strengths and weaknesses in ICT. Common areas students struggle with include programming concepts, network terminology and database management. We will identify these areas through diagnostic exercises and then practice targeted exercises. For example, if you struggle with HTML tags, you might practice creating different elements repeatedly until they become familiar.

Class activity:
Students will first complete a diagnostic test to identify their weak areas. Then they will work on targeted exercises for those specific areas, with teacher guidance available.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is your weakest area in ICT?
2. How can regular practice help improve your weak areas?
3. What resources can you use to learn more about difficult topics?
4. How will you track your progress in your weak areas?

Summary:
Focusing on our weaknesses helps us become more well-rounded ICT students.

topics.title: Typing mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to type accurately without looking at the keyboard, improve their typing speed.

Introduction:
Today we will practice typing skills. This is important for both the written and practical portions of the BECE exam.

Content:
Good typing skills make computer work faster and more efficient. We will focus on proper finger placement on the keyboard and building speed through regular practice. The home row keys are ASDF for the left hand and JKL; for the right hand. Nigerian examples could include typing practice with Nigerian names, cities or common phrases in local languages.

Class activity:
Students will complete timed typing exercises using online typing tutors. They will start with slow speed and gradually increase as accuracy improves. Each student will set a personal goal for speed and accuracy.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the home row keys on a keyboard?
2. Why is proper finger placement important for typing?
3. How can you improve your typing speed without sacrificing accuracy?
4. What is your current words per minute typing speed?

Summary:
Regular typing practice helps us work more efficiently on computer-based tasks.

topics.title: Coding mini project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to plan a simple coding project, write basic code to solve a problem.

Introduction:
Today we will work on a coding mini project. This builds on our earlier programming lessons and helps us apply coding concepts.

Content:
Coding is the process of creating instructions for computers to follow. For our mini project, we will use a visual programming language like Scratch or basic Python. The project should solve a simple problem, like creating a quiz about Nigerian history or a game that tests knowledge of Nigerian geography. Planning is important - we will first outline our project steps before writing any code.

Class activity:
Students will plan and create a simple coding project in pairs. Options include a quiz about Nigerian culture, a basic game featuring Nigerian landmarks, or a program that calculates exchange rates between Naira and other currencies.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the steps in planning a coding project?
2. Name two benefits of using visual programming languages.
3. How can you test if your code works correctly?
4. What coding project would you like to create next?

Summary:
Coding projects help us develop problem-solving skills and understand how programming works.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete ICT tasks quickly and accurately, demonstrate improved performance over time.

Introduction:
Today we will focus on improving both speed and accuracy in ICT tasks. This builds on our typing practice and coding projects.

Content:
Speed and accuracy are both important in ICT exams and real-world applications. We will practice completing tasks quickly while maintaining high accuracy. For example, in a spreadsheet task, you might practice entering data quickly but double-checking formulas for accuracy. Nigerian examples could include timed exercises with Nigerian market data or quick calculations involving currency conversions.

Class activity:
Students will complete a series of timed mini-tests covering different ICT skills. They will track their own progress and set goals for improvement in both speed and accuracy.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why are both speed and accuracy important in ICT tasks?
2. How can you improve your speed without losing accuracy?
3. What strategies help you stay focused during timed tasks?
4. Which ICT task do you find most challenging to complete quickly?

Summary:
Regular practice helps us develop the speed and accuracy needed for ICT success.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE mock exam under timed conditions, analyze their performance to identify remaining areas for improvement.

Introduction:
Today we will take our final mock examination. This comprehensive practice will help us prepare for the actual BECE ICT exam.

Content:
The final mock exam will replicate the actual BECE ICT exam as closely as possible. It will include theory questions, practical tasks and time limits for each section. The exam covers all topics we have studied this term including hardware, software, networks, programming and internet safety. Nigerian examples might include questions about using ICT in Nigerian schools or accessing government services like the National Identity Management System.

Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock examination under timed conditions. After completion, we will review answers together and discuss final preparation strategies.

Evaluation questions:
1. How did you prepare differently for this mock exam compared to earlier ones?
2. Which section did you perform best in and why?
3. What is your final strategy for the actual BECE exam?
4. How will you manage exam day stress?

Summary:
The final mock exam helps us build confidence and finalize our exam preparation.

topics.title: BECE readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list exam day tips, demonstrate proper exam techniques for success.

Introduction:
Today we will finalize our preparation for the BECE ICT exam. This concludes our term's work and focuses on exam success strategies.

Content:
Exam day success requires both preparation and good techniques. Important tips include getting enough sleep the night before, eating a good breakfast, arriving early at the exam center, reading all instructions carefully, managing time wisely and checking your work before submission. For Nigerian students, this might include planning for transportation to exam centers, especially in areas with traffic challenges like Lagos.

Class activity:
Students will create their personal exam day checklist and share one important tip with the class. We will also have a motivational send-off ceremony to build confidence.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are three important things to do the night before an exam?
2. How should you manage your time during the exam?
3. What should you do if you encounter a difficult question?
4. Why is it important to arrive early at the exam center?

Summary:
Proper preparation and exam techniques help us perform our best on exam day.
